sourceQualification.disposition: The build was produced from source commit 6bbf6915 with documentation-only working-tree changes. Executable application, package, build-script, dependency, fixture, and CI-workflow paths were unchanged from the independently reviewed executable baseline.

pointerClickModality.method: A physical pointer click with no drag was sent to row 1, column 1 on the readable Canvas.
observed: The selected-stitch status identified row 1, column 1.
The save status returned to Saved locally.

panThreshold.method: A pointer drag followed the viewport-coordinate path (128,436) -> (132,436) -> (135,436) -> (138,436), for 10 CSS px total movement.
observed: The gesture was treated as pan-only.
The previously selected row 1, column 1 remained selected and marked.
No new mark toggle or save transition was observed.
panThreshold.contract: Movement strictly greater than 6 CSS px is pan-only.

unreadableOverview.method: The viewer was reduced below READABLE_CELL_SIZE_CSS_PX and the Canvas was inspected visually and through the accessible status output before and after a pointer click.
observed: No glyph symbols were drawn or visually claimed.
The status said Zoom in to read symbols and mark stitches.
A pointer click did not change selection, mark state, or save state.

closeAndReopenPersistence.method: After row 1, column 1 was committed as marked, the application tab was closed. A new Chrome tab was created and the same local entry URL was opened.
observed: The X progress mark at row 1, column 1 was visibly restored without another toggle.

saveFailureVisualRollback.method: The registered browser-failure harness held the real per-project Web Lock. The application then received a pointer click attempting to unmark the committed row 1, column 1.
observed: The save status changed to Read-only.
The committed X remained visually present after the failed optimistic unmark.
After the failure harness released the lock and the application reloaded, the X was still present and the viewer returned to Saved locally.

verified: Chrome tab close and new-tab reopen

retention.note: The Chrome session was visually inspected and screenshots were displayed in the controlled Codex session, but no screenshot file was retained in the repository. DOM status and deterministic source/tests remain separately inspectable.
